neighbours.label: the comma right after an apology or interjection that opens a reply ('Sorry,', 'Well,', 'Okay,'), before the next clause
fire: She looked up from the desk and said, "Sorry, I didn't see you there."
When he asked about the money, I just said "Well, it's complicated."
He paused at the door. "Okay, we can leave now if you want."
I butted into their chat. "Sorry, that was rude of me."
The guide shrugged and replied, "Well, nobody really knows."
My brother groaned. "Fine, I'll do the dishes tonight."
She laughed at the question. "Honestly, I have no idea."
The clerk checked again. "Sorry, no rooms are left this week."
quiet: She looked up from the desk and said she had not seen him there.
When he asked about the money, I told him it was complicated.
He paused at the door and told us we could leave now.
I butted into their chat and felt rude about it later.
The guide shrugged, smiled, and replied that nobody really knew.
My brother groaned and agreed to do the dishes tonight.
She laughed at the question and admitted she had no idea.
The clerk checked again, but no rooms were left this week.

notes: logit effect promotes clause starters (' but', ' we', ' I') and suppresses another comma
